test_title: PYST 39: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In June 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) imposed a monetary penalty of ₹29.60 lakh (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakh Sixty Thousand only) on which of the following institutions for non-compliance with certain directions issued by RBI on ‘Licensing of Payments Banks’ on 6 June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fino Payments Bank Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, by an order dated **June 6, 2025**, has imposed a monetary penalty of **₹29.60 lakh** (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakh Sixty Thousand only) on **Fino Payments Bank Limited**.
 
• The penalty has been imposed in the exercise of powers vested in **RBI** under the provisions of **Section 47A(1)(c)** read with **Section 46(4)(i)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.
 
• The action was taken due to the bank's non-compliance with certain directions issued by **RBI** on **‘Licensing of Payments Banks’**.
 
• This regulatory action is based on deficiencies in **statutory and regulatory compliance** and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the bank with its customers.
 
• The **RBI** had conducted a statutory inspection for **Supervisory Evaluation** of the bank, which revealed violations related to the specific operating guidelines prescribed for **Payments Banks** in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fino Payments Bank Limited:**
 
 
• It was incorporated on **April 4, 2017**, after receiving the final license from the **Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• The bank is headquartered in **Navi Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Fino Payments Bank** emerged from **Fino Paytech Limited**, which was a pioneer in the **Business Correspondent (BC)** model for **Financial Inclusion**.
 
• The bank focuses on providing digital banking and payment services to the unbanked and under-banked population across **India**.
 
 
 
• **Payments Banks in India:**
 
 
• These are a specialized category of banks conceptualized by the **RBI** to further **Financial Inclusion**.
 
• They can accept **demand deposits** (currently up to **₹2 lakh** per individual customer) but are prohibited from lending or issuing credit cards.
 
• They mainly provide services such as **ATM/Debit cards**, **mobile banking**, **online fund transfers**, and **third-party insurance** products.
 
• Important examples include **Airtel Payments Bank**, **India Post Payments Bank**, and **Paytm Payments Bank**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• The **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, provides the legal framework for the regulation and supervision of the banking sector in **India**.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **RBI Act, 1934**, serves as the primary regulator for all scheduled commercial banks, including **Payments Banks**.
 
• Penalties are typically issued after a **Show Cause Notice (SCN)** is sent to the institution, and their oral or written submissions are considered by the **Central Bank**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **₹29.60 lakh** penalty highlights the **RBI's** stringent oversight regarding the **Licensing of Payments Banks** guidelines to ensure the stability of the **financial system**.
 
• Compliance with **RBI** directives is mandatory for all financial entities to prevent **operational risks** and maintain **customer trust**.
 
• Institutional transparency and adherence to **corporate governance** standards are key metrics monitored during the **RBI’s** annual **Supervisory Evaluation**.
